question.worked_solution:
The formula for the derivative of the inverse hyperbolic cosecant function is

$$
\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(\operatorname{arcsch}⁡x)=-\frac{1}{|x|\sqrt{1+{x}^{2}}}.
$$

Using the formula above with the chain rule, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x} & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(-2\operatorname{arcsch}⁡{x}^{2}) \\  & =-2\cdot \frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(\operatorname{arcsch}⁡{x}^{2}) \\  & =2\cdot \frac{1}{|{x}^{2}|\sqrt{1+({x}^{2})^{2}}}\cdot ({x}^{2})^{′} \\  & =2\cdot \frac{1}{{x}^{2}\sqrt{1+{x}^{4}}}\cdot 2x \\  & =\frac{4x}{{x}^{2}\sqrt{1+{x}^{4}}} \\  & =\frac{4}{x\sqrt{1+{x}^{4}}}.\end{aligned}
$$
